newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief aims for Cyprus settlement this year.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief aims for Cyprus settlement this year.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan is determined to intensify efforts to resolve the Cyprus question and to achieve an overall political solution this year, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Tuesday.

U.N. Cyprus mediator Han Sung-joo of South Korea, who is due in Cyprus on Wednesday, will discuss preparations for face-to-face talks in the coming months with leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, he said.

"The heightened tension in and around Cyprus have added urgency to the secretary-general's determination to intensify his efforts to address the substance of the Cyprus issue and achieve an overall political settlement in the course of this year," Eckhard said.

"This determination enjoys the support of the international community. The secretary-general has therefore instructed Professor Han to discuss with the leaders of the Cypriot communities preparations for face-to-face talks in the coming months."
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops landed in the north of the island in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.

U.N. efforts to reunite Cyprus under a federal system have so far failed. Tensions rose in recent weeks after the Cyprus government announced plans to buy Russian surface-to-air missiles and Turkey said it would take whatever action was needed to ensure they were not deployed.
